hints: Look closely at X on the right side of the cell. Notice it is a stack of membranes covered in tiny black dots and is continuous with the nucleus.
Recall what those tiny dots are, and remember that this organelle has two jobs: making something on its surface and moving it through its inner channels.
walkthrough:
**Identify Organelle X**

Look at the structure labelled X. It is a system of flattened membrane sacs covered in small dots.

Those dots are ribosomes, and membranes with ribosomes like this, joined to the nuclear envelope, are the rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER).

**Link Structure to Function**

Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, so proteins are made on the surface of the RER.

The folded new proteins then enter the lumen (the space inside the membranes) and are transported in vesicles toward the Golgi body.

**Choose the Complete Answer**

X does not just make proteins and it does not just move them. It does both jobs together.

That matches option B: protein synthesis and transport.

options.A: Lipid synthesis is the job of the smooth endoplasmic reticulum, which has no ribosomes. X is clearly rough with ribosomes.
options.B: X is rough endoplasmic reticulum. Its ribosomes synthesise proteins and its lumen transports them to the Golgi in vesicles.
options.C: Protein synthesis does happen on the ribosomes of X, but this is incomplete because X also transports proteins through its membranes.
options.D: Protein transport does happen inside X, but this is incomplete because the ribosomes on X also carry out protein synthesis.
